beats.care: Check parcel status only on the courier's official site or app. If you lose money, call 1930 right away.
beats.what: The Telangana Cyber Security Bureau warned people about fake delivery messages on World Post Day, 9 October.
beats.why: Scammers pose as couriers or postal services, claiming a parcel is stuck over an address error or unpaid fee, to make you click and pay.

cards.body: The messages say your parcel is held for a wrong address, customs charges or an unpaid delivery fee, with a link to 'fix' it. The link steals card details or OTPs. TGCSB says: verify first, never pay through unknown links, and block and report the number.
Call immediately if you've lost money, and file a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in.
cards.caption: National cybercrime helpline

cards.body: They create panic and urgency: a tiny fee, a ticking deadline, a parcel you might actually be expecting. That rush is exactly what makes people skip checking. Pause, and the scam falls apart.

cards.q: A text says your parcel is on hold. What's the safest move?
cards.why: Scam links rely on you acting fast, so going straight to the official site cuts them out completely.
